Proven by an EXECUTED Playwright run on WebKit, where the race reproduces, rather than only on Chromium where it does not. Separately the spec addresses the result heading exactly rather than by substring, because role-name matching is substring by default and a query equal to a title matches both the results heading and the card heading -- a spec defect that only appeared once the suite was first executed.

tasks.notes: IMPLEMENTED IN THE TREE AND NEVER CLAIMED, like the rest of recovery packet 1 -- but PARTIALLY, and the two gaps are different in kind. This is the fifth task found in that state, and its code landed while it sat BACKLOG and unowned: control/events.jsonl records apps/web/src/app/loading.tsx and page.tsx being edited as belonging to PL-0704 while it was blocked on a lifecycle dependency. So it must be started with --reconcile-existing, never against HEAD. IT IS A MODIFICATION TASK IN THE REVIEWER'S TAXONOMY, MOSTLY, and that changes the probe. Its central act was a DELETION -- the root loading.tsx removed -- and marker absence cannot witness a deletion. What it also did, and what CAN be witnessed, is introduce two named components where anonymous route-level skeletons used to be: CatalogSkeleton in app/page.tsx and PlaybackLoading in app/watch/[contentId]/page.tsx, each now a Suspense fallback sitting BELOW the existence decision rather than a loading file wrapping the whole segment. Those two names are new even though their markup is not, so a pickaxe on the names finds the relocation, which is precisely this task's work. Use them as the witnesses; do not use the deleted file. TWO GAPS AGAINST THE ACCEPTANCE, AND ONLY ONE IS A CODE GAP. FIRST, THE TITLE SKELETON, WHICH I BELIEVE IS A CONTRACT GAP RATHER THAN A DEFECT AND AM FLAGGING FOR A RULING RATHER THAN FIXING. The acceptance says any fix must KEEP the loading skeletons rather than deleting them to move a status code. Home and watch comply: both relocated their skeleton into a Suspense boundary below a cheap existence check that consults nobody. The title route did not -- it deleted its skeleton outright -- and its own header argues why: on that route a status line precedes the first body byte, so no byte may be sent before the catalog answers whether the title exists, which is the definition of having nothing to stream. A full-page skeleton there IS the defect the task exists to remove. The only honest way to restore one would be a section whose data does not depend on the title existing, and none exists today. So the code looks right and the clause looks over-general. I am not rewriting the acceptance to match the code unasked -- that is the move the reviewer has twice had to authorise explicitly, on PL-0205's wording and on PL-0706's -- so it is proposed here and left for the verdict. SECOND, THE PRODUCTION-MODE 404, WHICH IS NOT THIS TASK'S TO CLOSE. An unknown title answers 404 under development and 200 with a refusal panel under production, and that is correct rather than broken: on a hosted build no catalog metadata source is constructible, so loadTitleDetail reports error rather than not-found, notFound() is unreachable, and a build that answered 404 there would be claiming an absence it never looked for. The precondition is a catalog source that exists in a deployment, which is PL-0305's, now READY since PL-0105 completed. ALLOWEDPATHS CORRECTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. apps/web/src/app/(home)/** is DROPPED: it is a dead declaration for a route-group approach that was considered and rejected, it reserves a directory that does not exist, and it starves nothing only by accident. apps/web/src/app/loading.tsx is KEPT even though the file is deleted, because the deletion is the change and a surface that omitted it would not fingerprint the task's central act. TWO PATHS ADDED. docs/E2E.md, because it and .github/workflows/ci.yml currently CONTRADICT EACH OTHER about whether the two 404 assertions have ever been observed passing -- E2E.md claims an executed 2026-09-05 pass on all four browser projects, ci.yml says UNKNOWN, expected to pass, never observed passing -- and settling that is exactly what this task's EXECUTED clause is about. It is declared by PL-0706, which is DONE, and by PL-0703, which is BLOCKED, so no active conflict. And .github/workflows/ci.yml, which UNTIL NOW WAS DECLARED BY NO TASK IN THE REPOSITORY AT ALL: every CI change this project has made has landed outside every declared surface. That is a real declaration hole rather than a convenience, and this task adopting it is a partial fix at best -- the file is repository governance rather than frontend, and it should eventually belong to whatever task adopts CLAUDE.md and control/README.md, which are undeclared for the same reason.

The cause is that a segment's loading file wraps that segment in Suspense, so React flushes the shell at 200 before the access-fallback error escapes the render and Next can set the status; the root loading file wraps every route in the application, so per-route fixes alone are insufficient. THE SKELETON CLAUSE, AMENDED. Any fix must RELOCATE the loading skeletons below the existence decision rather than deleting them to move a status code, ON EVERY ROUTE WHERE A SECTION'S DATA DOES NOT DEPEND ON THE ADDRESS EXISTING. The title route is exempt, and the exemption is reasoned rather than granted: a well-formed unknown title id is indistinguishable from a real one until the catalog answers, the status line precedes the first body byte, so no byte may be sent before that load resolves -- which is the definition of having nothing to stream. A full-page skeleton there IS the defect this task exists to remove, so the unamended clause required the defect on one of the three routes it governs. The exemption is EMPIRICAL AND REVERSIBLE, not permanent: the moment the title page grows a section whose data does not depend on the title existing -- recommendations, continue-watching, anything PL-0301 or PL-0501 fetches separately -- it gains an in-page Suspense below the decision exactly as the watch route has, and this clause binds again. tasks.notes: THE REVIEWER'S OWN CARVE-OUT FROM THE PL-0203 APPROVAL, not a finding of this lane's. gpt-architect approved PL-0203's script/trim corrective and, in the same verdict, identified this as a genuinely separate defect and agreed it should be its own cross-lane media task covering both audio and subtitles. In substance: the zh-yue / zh-cmn instinct points at it, but it is not a script issue -- those are Cantonese and Mandarin extended-language/macrolanguage distinctions; RFC 5646 specifically notes that the Chinese languages encompassed by zh are generally not mutually intelligible when spoken, so a matcher that collapses both to primary zh can call the wrong SPOKEN language a preferred-language fallback. The reviewer proposed P0 and stated explicitly that this does not invalidate the script/trim corrective PL-0203 landed. IT IS DISTINCT FROM THAT SCRIPT RULE, and the distinction is the whole task: a script subtag identifies a WRITING SYSTEM, which is why require_compatible_script is right for automatic subtitle selection and deliberately looser for audio; this is about MUTUAL INTELLIGIBILITY OF SPEECH, an audio-first fact that reaches subtitles only because both surfaces share one matcher. It depends on PL-0203 rather than racing it because it corrects the same function -- languageMatch in packages/media-engine/src/audio.ts, which subtitles.ts imports -- and two concurrent owners of that function would collide. Provenance of the verdict is the same as PL-0203's review record: transcribed by Claude from the ChatGPT review session rather than received over the agent bus. IMPLEMENTED IN ROUND 45, AND IT IS THE ONLY TASK IN THE RECOVERY CAMPAIGN THAT NEEDED NO PROVENANCE WORK AT ALL -- genuinely unstarted, so an ordinary start captures a true base. THE RULE IS STRUCTURAL, WITH NO REGISTRY VENDORED, exactly as the script rule already is. A new spokenLanguage helper answers which language will come out of the speakers rather than which subtag a string starts with, and it differs from primarySubtag in precisely one place: where a macrolanguage has been narrowed by an extended-language subtag. BCP-47 spells a language as 2*3ALPHA optionally followed by an extlang of exactly 3ALPHA, while a region is two letters or three DIGITS and a script is four letters, so three ASCII letters immediately after a two- or three-letter primary is unambiguously an extlang and nothing else can take that shape in that position. RFC 5646 permanently invalidates the second and third extlang positions, so there is at most one to find. THE COLLAPSE RUNS TOWARD THE SPECIFIC RATHER THAN THE GENERAL, which is what makes the equivalence clause work in both directions: zh-cmn becomes cmn rather than zh, so the prefixed and bare spellings of one language agree, and the equivalence survives any region or script suffix because those subtags are never consulted. A bare zh stays zh -- it names the macrolanguage and neither variety, so treating it as either would invent a preference the viewer did not express, which is the same asymmetry the script rule uses when it says a tag naming no script conflicts with nothing. THE NEW OUTCOME IS ITS OWN REASON, as the acceptance requires: preferred_language_other_variety_only, distinct from preferred_language_other_script_only and from the regional fallback, because the three have different remedies -- a script conflict is about READING and the dialogue is still the viewer's, a regional difference is cosmetic and is still selected, and this one is the wrong language. Reporting it as a regional fallback would move the defect out of the matcher and into the vocabulary. ONE THING WORTH KNOWING THAT THE DESIGN MADE TRUE BY ACCIDENT AND THE TESTS NOW PIN: the script and variety findings are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE rather than merely ordered. matchesOnlyAcrossScripts requires a match under ignore_script, setting the script aside leaves the spoken-language comparison, and a different variety fails it -- so zh-yue-Hant against a zh-cmn-Hans preference is not across both boundaries, it is simply the wrong language and the script question is moot. Only a track in the viewer's own spoken language can be across the script boundary, which is the only case where a font is the remedy. EXERCISED THROUGH BOTH CONSUMERS, which the acceptance demands because the two share one comparator precisely so they cannot drift, and the way that guarantee fails is one being corrected while the other keeps the old behaviour. selectAudioTrack is asserted not to hand a Mandarin listener a six-channel Cantonese track that would have won on quality had the language matched, and selectSubtitleTrack is asserted to refuse a Cantonese subtitle under the new reason while still returning it in ordered for a player to offer. TWO PROPERTIES HAD TO BE TIGHTENED RATHER THAN MERELY KEPT PASSING, and that is the most useful thing this task turned up. Both audio.property.test.ts and subtitles.property.test.ts asserted that a matched pair shares a PRIMARY SUBTAG, which was a restatement of the rule being removed; once zh-cmn and cmn are both in languageTagArb it is simply false, since that is one spoken language with two primary subtags. Both now ask spokenLanguage, which is the stronger claim and the one the matcher actually makes. The arbitrary gained zh, zh-cmn, zh-yue, cmn and yue-hk so the property suites reach the new path at all -- without that they would have kept passing while testing nothing about it. The three contracts entries are where the language vocabulary this task corrects actually lives -- domains/subtitles.ts carries the subtitle policy and its outcome vocabulary, domains/audio.ts the track contract, and testing/arbitraries.ts the language-tag generators the property suites draw from. Narrowed on a PREDICTION rather than on a diff, unlike PL-0204's and PL-0205's, because this task is not yet written: if the correction turns out to want a new shared leaf -- a language-tag vocabulary of its own, say -- that is a deliberate widening at claim time with a line in this field, which is the ordinary path and is cheaper than a wildcard that reserves a whole package. packages/media-engine/** stays wide: this task owns the matcher and both its consumers, and it shares an owner with PL-0204 and PL-0205.

tasks.notes: BLOCKER 1, AND IT IS THE PL-0706 DEFECT IN A SECOND PLACE. ProfileScope carries a type-only unique symbol property while mintProfileScope returns an ordinary object via cast, so a caller holding a genuine scope can write a spread with a replacement profileId and TypeScript carries the branded structural type straight through -- without the explicit cast ADR-007 claims is the only forgery route. Downstream persistence then trusts scope.profileId directly, which makes this a cross-profile data-access bypass rather than a typing nicety. The prescription: make the scope genuinely nominal so a spread copy cannot remain assignable, and if it is meant to be a runtime capability rather than a compile-time proof, use issuance identity as well. The pattern already exists in this repository twice -- ClassifiedRuntime in packages/contracts/src/shared/runtime.ts and PinnedTarget in media-inspection -- module-private brand, freeze, WeakSet registry, identity check as the consumer's first action. THE SURFACE THIS IMPLIES IS WIDER THAN THIS TASK CURRENTLY DECLARES, AND THAT IS SETTLED BEFORE THE CLAIM RATHER THAN DISCOVERED DURING IT. The reviewer offered two levels: at minimum make the scope genuinely nominal so a spread copy cannot remain assignable, and if it is meant to be a runtime capability, use issuance identity as well. The minimum is NOT ACHIEVABLE IN THE TYPE SYSTEM, and PL-0706 already established why: a spread copies a branded property along with everything else and type-checks with no cast at all, so only object identity rejects it. TypeScript cannot make a spread unassignable. Therefore the runtime registry is not the optional upper level here, it is the only level that works -- and a registry closes nothing unless the consumers ASK. The consumers are in another package: packages/persistence/src/progress-repository.ts and watchlist-repository.ts read scope.profileId straight into their predicates, and profile-repository.ts and repository-scoping.test.ts also handle the type. So this task must declare packages/persistence/src/** as a write path when it is claimed, not merely the migration, and it will then overlap PL-0402, PL-0403 and PL-0404, which are BACKLOG today and must be sequenced after it. The alternative -- brand and registry in packages/auth with no consumer asking -- would produce a capability that looks unforgeable and is not, which is worse than the present state because it would read as fixed. Whoever claims this should widen the declaration in the same edit that claims it, and say so in the reason. BLOCKER 2, AND THE EXACT PIN IS WORKING RATHER THAN FAILING. better-auth and its Drizzle adapter are pinned at exactly 1.7.1. Upstream's current release is 1.7.4, from 2026-09-10, and its security policy supports only the latest version. The reviewer was explicit that this is not an argument against exact pins: it proves the policy works by making staleness visible, which is what ADR-007 said it was for. Move both packages together and update REVIEWED_BETTER_AUTH_VERSION. DO NOT BUMP AND LEAVE THE MIGRATION: 1.7.3 restored the 1.6 account core schema after the issuer-schema change in 1.7.0 through 1.7.2, while this repository's hand-written migration still has an issuer column and an (issuer, account_id) uniqueness rule. The migration must be regenerated or reconciled against the reviewed version BEFORE security approval. That is why packages/persistence/migrations/0000_profile_scoped_identity.sql moves from reviewDependency to WRITE PATH here: on PL-0401 it was only evidence, and read-only was correct; here it has to change, and reviewDependencies are read-only by contract. PL-0402 also owns packages/persistence and is BACKLOG, so no active conflict exists today, but the two must be sequenced and the reviewer should say which owns that file afterwards. BLOCKER 3. ADR-007 still states obsolete control-plane routing, naming gpt-architect as preferred implementer and claude-lead as reviewer, while the record now correctly has claude-backend implementing and gpt-architect reviewing independently. Rewrite that paragraph as history rather than as current routing, and prefer wording that points at the task gate as authoritative -- otherwise completing the review needs a post-approval edit that immediately stales the fingerprint it just bound. TWO HONEST CAVEATS CARRIED FORWARD FROM PL-0401, neither an unmet clause: the migration has never been executed, because no PostgreSQL exists in this environment, and better-auth.ts is deliberately untested. SEQUENCING: this task is READY rather than BLOCKED because nothing external gates it, but it should not be claimed until the three blockers are implemented, and claiming it early would reserve packages/auth and two documents while no work was happening.

The commander ruled on 2026-09-15 that all profile ids must flow through the same validated accessor as the production repositories. tasks.title: Supersession is a field, and a task cannot stay gated behind one
tasks.description: Four tasks -- PL-0205, PL-0401, PL-0601, PL-0703 -- are BLOCKED, terminal, and superseded by a corrective re-run. Each says so only in prose. BLOCKED transitions only to BACKLOG, READY or CANCELED, so a superseded task can never reach DONE, and with completion.requireAllDependenciesDone true, any task depending on one is gated forever. That is not a hypothetical: PL-0301 was gated behind PL-0205 while PL-0207 sat DONE, and with it PL-0302, PL-0501, PL-0502, PL-0701 and PL-0702. A human noticed. Nothing in ai:validate could have.
tasks.notes: SCOPE IS THE VALIDATOR, NOT A DEPENDENCY REWRITER. The rule reports; it never edits a dependency, because repointing a dependency is a task-definition change and those are deliberate, reasoned and recorded -- see PL-0301's own notes for what that looks like. An automatic repointer would make the graph self-modifying on the strength of a field any writer can set. THE RULE, PRECISELY. For each task T declaring supersededBy S: S must exist, must not be T, and T must not itself be DONE, or that is an ERROR, because a DONE task that claims to be superseded is two contradictory records of the same work. If S declares supersedes, it must name T -- a one-way pointer is a typo waiting to be trusted. Then, for each task D whose dependencies contain T: if S is DONE, ERROR, because D is gated behind a task that can never complete while its replacement already has; if S is not DONE, WARN, because the edge is not yet fatal but will become so the moment S completes, and a warning that arrives before the deadlock is the entire point. WHY ERROR AND NOT WARN FOR THE FIRST CASE. ai:validate already treats provenance drift as a warning and structural impossibility as an error. A dependency that can never be satisfied is structural: no sequence of legal transitions resolves it. It belongs with 'missing dependency' and 'invalid status', not with drift. WHAT THIS RULE CANNOT DO, STATED SO NOBODY OVERTRUSTS IT. supersededBy is self-asserted, exactly like fromAgent on the agent bus. It proves that somebody wrote a pointer, not that the successor genuinely carries the predecessor's work. A wrong pointer produces a wrong error or hides a real deadlock. It is a cheap alarm on a failure mode that has already cost this project one stalled milestone, not a proof of anything.
tasks.acceptance: ai:validate refuses a task graph in which a task depends on a task that declares supersededBy and whose named successor is DONE, and warns when the successor is not yet DONE. It also refuses a supersededBy naming a missing task, naming itself, declared on a DONE task, or contradicted by the successor's supersedes field. The rule reports and never edits a dependency. The four existing supersession pairs validate clean, and a regression in scripts/test-ai-control-plane.mjs proves the rule fires -- both that it errors on a reconstructed PL-0301-behind-PL-0205 graph and that it stays silent on the repaired one, so it cannot pass by being inert.

tasks.title: Windows desktop shell and the PlayerAdapter boundary
tasks.description: Project Liberty's first production target is Windows desktop on the commander's own machine. The commander has settled the direction: a Tauri shell, the existing Next.js application preserved rather than rewritten and served by a Next standalone sidecar, a PlayerAdapter boundary the application and domain layers depend on instead of any concrete player, libmpv for compatible non-DRM playback, Shaka/EME retained for DRM-capable playback, capability routing made explicit before playback rather than discovered during it, and an LGPL-compatible libmpv/FFmpeg build pipeline of our own rather than a GPL prebuilt. This task records that decision and specifies the boundary. It writes documentation only -- no shell, no adapter, no dependency is added here, because the instruction is that architecture is recorded before a large irreversible implementation, not after it.
tasks.notes: THE AUDIT CAME FIRST AND IT FOUND A CLEAN SLATE. A repository-wide search for electron, tauri, mpv, libmpv, webview2, neutralino and nw.js across every .ts, .tsx, .json, .md, .mjs and .yml outside node_modules returned nothing. So neither shell was favoured by anything already in the tree, and the decision was made on evidence rather than on inertia. Today's player is shaka-player ~5.2.6 with xstate ^5.32.5 and custom-media-element in apps/web. THE DECIDING FACT IS COMPOSITING, NOT BUNDLE SIZE. Putting HTML chrome over a hardware-accelerated native video surface in one window on Windows is a documented, shipping arrangement on WebView2 -- ICoreWebView2Controller2::put_DefaultBackgroundColor accepts alpha 0 or 255 only, and at 0 the host's content renders beneath -- and has no supported path on Chromium, where PPAPI is gone and child HWNDs are no longer in the window hierarchy. Stremio ships the WebView2 plus libmpv --wid arrangement in production on Windows and measured its previous render-API-into-a-texture approach as 2-5x worse. Any size-based argument for Tauri should be dropped: with a Node sidecar the installer lands near Electron's anyway. THE SIDECAR IS WHAT PRESERVES THE APPLICATION. Tauri's default is a static export, which would force every /api/v1 route handler off Next -- a rewrite of the application's architecture, which the instruction forbids. output: standalone in a sidecar keeps Server Components, route handlers, proxy.ts, cookies(), headers(), Server Actions and ISR working. It costs a Node runtime in the bundle, a loopback listener, supervision code and Tauri's CSP injection, which does not reach an external http origin. ONE QUESTION THIS TASK DOES NOT DECIDE AND MUST NOT DECIDE SILENTLY. A sidecar runs the application's server on a machine the user administers. If provider resolution runs there, then the boundary that enforces invariants 1 and 2 executes from files the user can read and replace, with whatever credentials it needs in its environment. The alternative is that the desktop build implements those specific routes as an authenticated proxy to the backend -- same route, same contract, same URL, a different implementation behind it, selected by build target, which is ordinary adapter work rather than a rewrite. This document states the question, states the recommendation, and leaves the ruling to the reviewer and the commander. It is a design input to PL-0501 and is cheaper to supply now than to retrofit. DRM IS A ROUTING CONSTRAINT, NOT A GAP TO CLOSE. mpv has no CDM and cannot be given one. That is not something to work around: the mpv adapter must REFUSE a DRM-protected candidate with a named reason and must never attempt it, never fall back and never degrade. Which means capability routing has to be an explicit, reasoned decision before playback -- canPlay returning a reason on both branches -- rather than a guess discovered at load time. That is what makes invariant 2 structural here rather than a promise, and it is why the boundary carries a capability descriptor at all. THE LICENSING WORK IS THE LONG POLE AND IT GATES SHIPPING RATHER THAN PROTOTYPING. A stock prebuilt libmpv is a GPL build and must not ship in a closed-source product; the one LGPL variant on offer statically links an LGPLv3 FFmpeg and carries its builder's own no-warranty disclaimer. Building our own with -Dgpl=false and an LGPL FFmpeg, with an SBOM, converts an open-ended exposure into a reviewable artifact. Nothing in this document is legal advice and counsel review is named as a precondition of shipping rather than assumed.
tasks.acceptance: A recorded architecture decision states the Windows desktop target, the Tauri shell, the preserved Next.js application served by a standalone sidecar, and the LGPL-compatible libmpv/FFmpeg build pipeline, each with the evidence it rests on and the strongest argument against it. It specifies PlayerAdapter as an interface the application and domain layers depend on -- load an authorized playback session, play, pause, seek, stop, select audio track, select subtitle track, set volume, expose position and duration, expose buffering and stall events, expose recoverable and fatal errors, expose track metadata, expose A/V sync telemetry where available, dispose -- with no mpv, Electron, Tauri or Shaka type reachable from it, and names the two implementations behind it and the explicit capability routing that chooses between them, including the requirement that the mpv adapter refuse DRM-protected candidates with a named reason rather than attempt them. It states that media addresses continue to come only from authorized provider resolution and the playback-session boundary and that the client can never submit one, that stream candidate ranking stays in @liberty/media-engine, and that provider-specific logic stays in @liberty/provider-sdk. It states where provider resolution runs in the desktop build as an open question with a recommendation rather than deciding it silently, because that answer is a design input to PL-0501. It records what was verified, what was not, and which specific facts would reverse each decision. No shell, adapter or dependency is implemented here.

tasks.title: An engine-unavailable reason that can say libmpv did not load
tasks.description: EngineUnavailableReason in apps/web/src/components/player/playback-controller.ts is Shaka-shaped. Its members describe a browser that cannot run the web engine, and browser_unsupported is a misnomer the moment the engine is a native library in a desktop shell rather than a script in a page. There is no member that means the native player failed to load. A NativePlayerAdapter would have to report a false reason or invent one locally, and either makes the failure less debuggable than the web path it sits beside.
tasks.notes: THE VOCABULARY, NOT A NEW MEMBER. Adding a libmpv_unavailable member beside browser_unsupported would leave the union naming one engine's failure modes and one library's, which is the same coupling one layer up. The question for the reviewer is whether the reason should describe WHAT FAILED in engine-neutral terms -- the engine could not be loaded, the platform cannot run this engine, the engine loaded and refused this source -- with the engine's own detail carried beside it rather than encoded in the member name. COUPLED TO PL-0904 AND DELIBERATELY SEPARATE. Both are the same observation in two places: the player's error vocabulary assumes Shaka. They are separate tasks because they have different consumers -- unavailability is a startup decision the controller makes before any source is loaded, while a playback error is a per-attempt outcome the failover scheduler classifies -- and because merging them would put one review range across two behaviours. Whoever takes the second should read the first's verdict. DO NOT BREAK THE FAILOVER CLASSIFICATION. packages/media-engine consumes playback failures and treats network_transient as the only retryable class; an unavailability reason that leaks into that path as retryable would make the player retry a library that is not installed.
tasks.acceptance: The engine-unavailable vocabulary can represent a native engine failing to load without naming Shaka, a browser or libmpv in the member itself, and the existing web reasons keep their present meaning and their present tests. An engine's own detail is carried beside the reason rather than encoded in it. No unavailability reason reaches the failover scheduler as retryable. The rename or widening is proven by a regression that fails if browser_unsupported is reintroduced as the only way to say an engine is missing.

tasks.title: Playback errors carry an origin, so a native failure is not a Shaka number
tasks.description: PlaybackError in apps/web/src/components/player/shaka-error.ts carries code and category pinned to Shaka 5.2.x numbering. A native adapter has no such numbers: libmpv reports MPV_EVENT_END_FILE with a reason and an error field, on an entirely different scale. Today a NativePlayerAdapter must either report null in both fields, which discards the only diagnostic it has, or borrow a Shaka number that means something else, which is worse. PL-0901 requires the adapter boundary to expose recoverable and fatal errors without leaking an engine type, and this is where that leaks.
tasks.notes: AN ORIGIN, SO THE NUMBER MEANS SOMETHING. The proposal the desktop document records is that an error names the engine that produced it, and that its engine-specific code is read only in that origin's terms. The reviewer should also rule on whether the classification the failover scheduler consumes -- rights, decode, source_unavailable, network_transient -- stays engine-neutral and is derived per origin, which is the shape that keeps packages/media-engine from learning about either engine. AN HONEST CONSEQUENCE, RECORDED BEFORE IT IS DISCOVERED. mpv's END_FILE error is coarser than Shaka's code pairs, so a native origin will legitimately classify to unknown more often. The scheduler already handles that: an unclassified charged attempt cannot silently reset the budget, and attemptsByCandidate and attempt_failed_unclassified exist for exactly this. Do not manufacture a false classification to avoid the unknown branch -- PL-0204's approval turned on the budget being honest about what it could not classify. COUPLED TO PL-0903, SEPARATE FOR THE REASON RECORDED THERE.
tasks.acceptance: A playback error names the origin that produced it, and an engine-specific code is interpretable only against that origin rather than being read on one engine's numbering. A native error can be represented without borrowing a Shaka code and without discarding the detail the engine did supply. The classification packages/media-engine consumes stays engine-neutral, derived per origin, and unchanged in meaning for every existing Shaka case, proven by the existing shaka-error regressions continuing to pass unmodified. An error that cannot be classified stays unclassified rather than being assigned a plausible class.
